headline: A new long-form is uploaded and scheduled, “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN”. It is not the Ravana long-form, which is due on 19 November with no draft on disk. The newest film Short is behind the usual on day two, a sign the film window is closing.

top3.topic: Ramayana film, twelve days in: takings falling, reading still up
top3.signal: Box-office headlines today report a steep fall on the second Monday; the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is still at 2.85x its median. The radar's step for this week is the fact-check long-form.
top3.recommendation: This is decision 1, and the window will not wait past this week. Do not let the Indonesia launch push the Ravana long-form past 19 November. The hour it publishes, pin it under the three Ravana Shorts. Judge it on day three.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: three days, no Short scripted
top3.signal: The Karnataka row over his legacy has been in the news since 11 November (correction: yesterday's brief said 10 November). The radar's step for this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”.
top3.source: Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November
top3.recommendation: Decision 2, in dates: script today, record 18 November, publish Friday 20 November an hour or two before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. Keep “Tipu Sultan” at the front of the title.

top3.topic: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November: the radar's step is due now
top3.signal: The top-ranked dated moment, seven days out; the radar's step is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The radar also lists Tarabai imprisoning Rajaram II on the same date.
top3.recommendation: Decision 3, in dates: script by 19 November, record by 21, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. The working title now carries his name. Skip the Tarabai date: it makes the heroine of one of the channel's biggest Shorts the villain, its date comes from a low-confidence list, and one Short per date is enough.

more.signal: On the radar thirteen days out. This week's step is research with named sources; the next, on 23 November, is a script. The channel's earlier Churchill Short failed on its opening.
more.recommendation: Not a decision yet. Collect named sources for one Churchill order this week; on 23 November, with the Tipu and Tegh Bahadur Shorts out, decide whether it becomes a Short. No long-form on this date: the Ravana long-form holds the slot.

more.topic: Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, in cinemas 4 December
more.signal: A Salman Khan war film whose trailer leads the YouTube chart rows the tracker flagged this week. The radar has no confirmed subject for it.
more.recommendation: Check what real event, if any, the film is about before 20 November, when its first step opens. If it is a real war with an Indian side and a named enemy, it is the next mass-release peg; if it is fiction, skip it.

skipped.topic: Owner pick: “Ramayana is itihasa, not mythology”
skipped.signal: Chosen by the owner on 15 November. Itiha's “Itihasa vs Myth” Short of 3 November stands at 77 views.
skipped.source: Owner's note of 15 November, own Analytics
skipped.recommendation: Not a YouTube Short again; the owner's note sends it to Instagram. See the Instagram section.

whats_working: The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11.9 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Ravana long-form's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”

A second Ramayana long-form is ready: “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” is uploaded and scheduled. Its title states a claim, the check both earlier Ramayana long-forms failed in their post-mortems.

“Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” keeps earning from search: 9,426 views, with steady daily views for ten days and no decay, as searches for “ram setu” and “adams bridge” land on it. A Short that answers a searched name keeps working.
whats_wrong: Long-form has run down and the last release did not stop it. “Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,324 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000, 8 days after release. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: the Indonesia long-form. At day three, compare its first drop after the opening with the 14 points “Ramayana’s Many Versions” lost at 0:35.

Film reach is still not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.5, and only 41.3% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are now counted. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Ravana long-form, which names one; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Asia long-form's.

The newest film Short is behind the usual on day two: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” has 1,387 views at 31.7 an hour, far behind the Ravana Shorts at the same age. Probable cause: the film's audience is thinning (takings fell steeply on its second Monday) and the title is about the film's rule, not a person. Test: day three, 18 November. If it is still under the usual, the film window is closed for Shorts; make no more and give the time to Tipu and Tegh Bahadur.

actions.action: When “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” goes public, pin one comment under “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” that answers the Chola correction in a line and points to the new video, and send the new video out on WhatsApp the same day.
actions.rationale: The Asia long-form is the channel's largest long-form audience, at 348.7 views an hour averaged since release, and the Chola point is its most-liked correction. WhatsApp is the largest outside source of views.

actions.action: Look up the Indonesia long-form's scheduled time in Studio and keep at least a day between it and the Ravana long-form.
actions.rationale: Each long-form is judged on day three; two going up together blur both readings.

actions.action: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.
actions.rationale: They stand at 77 and 255 views two weeks on, with days of zero after publish. Still open.

actions.action: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.
actions.rationale: Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.

growth.verdict: Needs 226 net subscribers a day. The channel does 36.15/day, so the target is a **6.2x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter"), reaches 37.1/day — still 6.1x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2032-12-18, 6.1 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1276 of the 2,821 subscribers that 21 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 17/day (476 of 940 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 21 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 38.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 32 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 134, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 451 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 17/day (476 of 940 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 8 revision long-form videos, median 58 subscribers, against 32 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 17/day (476 of 940 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,276 subscribers on 72,871 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
